text:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT: svc-inference - elevated 5xx + streaming errors concentrated in az1a (us-west-2a). Paging oncall @maya. Correlation hint: resolver latency + egress packet loss. Link: https://pagerduty/INC12345
maya: on it, joining. creating this channel for live coord
jon: i'm looking at traceroutes from router -> resolver -> instance. starting pcap on a sample host
leo: seeing sustained egress packet loss ~20-40% from host ENIs in az1a to internet. RTTs fine but drops on TX
rachel: runtime spikes: KV cache misses, repeated gRPC reconnects, clients backoff failing. token churn through the roof
maya: immediate mitigations we can run now?
jon: suggest 1) shift routing preference away from az1a to az1b/az1c 2) reduce retry budgets + drop long streaming sessions 3) throttle heavy QPS customers as temporary measure
leo: initiating router policy change to prefer cross-az backends. will post the command i'm running: `curl -sS -X POST https://router.internal/config -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"route_preference":["az1b","az1c","az1a"]}'`
infra-bot: autoscaler: provisioning +6 ephemeral inference nodes in az1b to receive shifted traffic (request id: as-7721)
cust-ops: marking high-QPS tenants: acme-inc, betaapp, delta-ml. prepping customer notifications, ETA for message 10m
statusbot: creating status page incident "Degraded inference in us-west-2a" — will update every 15m
maya: enable model-fallback for latency sensitive routes while we stabilize (small-v2 or quantized variant). patching runtime route config now
rachel: pushing fallback: `PATCH /v1/routes/stream {"fallback_model":"small-v2","max_context_tokens":512}` — will cut memory and speed up recovery
jon: NLB health checks to backend pool were flapping — increased healthcheck window to 30s and reduced threshold to 3 consecutive successes
leo: opened ticket with cloud provider — they report anomalies on a subset of AZ egress NAT instances; investigating NIC-level packet drops. no ETA yet
maya: drain plan for affected compute: cordon + drain 8 nodes in az1a to prevent accepting new requests while router shifts. runbook step: `kubectl drain node/<name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
infra-bot: drain jobs kicked off for nodes: node-az1a-045, node-az1a-052, node-az1a-061
jon: monitoring dashboard: target is -70% 5xx within 10m after reroute. I'll post updates every 2m
-- 8 minutes later --
rachel: metrics: 5xx reduced ~55%, streaming reconnects down 45%. tail latency for fallback routes improved ~40%
leo: provider says they see anomalous NIC telemetry; they'll try a failover of the NAT gateway and escalate to infra team. still awaiting root cause
cust-ops: notifications sent to enterprise contacts. CS has updated tickets for acme-inc and betaapp with mitigation steps and ETA for next update 30m
maya: keep model-fallback and routing preference for now. Ops checklist: (1) keep router pref to az1b for 2h (2) continue node drains in az1a (3) do not re-add drained nodes until provider confirms egress stability
ops-lead: acknowledged — i'll take watch. will coordinate with provider POC and start a second wave of capacity if we see secondary spikes
jon: logging note: created incident log + PM link: https://confluence/incidents/INC12345-postmortem — please add timeline entries and attach pcap dump
statusbot: status updated: "Partial recovery — mitigation in place (traffic shifted, fallbacks enabled). We are monitoring."
maya: handing incident to @ops-lead for sustained watch. will remain on-call for escalation for 1h then sign off. great triage everyone. :white_check_mark:
